changes.rationale: Owner decision (Phase 2D). P1 said "every no-param endpoint rejects any query". Five endpoints (alerts, config, csp-report, telegram, link/verify) never read the query at all. The threat of the control (scope confusion / HTTP parameter pollution, ASVS V15.3.7) is that a parameter changes authority, scope or the selected object; a parameter that is provably never read cannot do that. The wording is normalised to the security property: an unexpected parameter is rejected OR demonstrably ignored, where "demonstrably" means a behavioural differential (identical response and identical dependency calls with and without hostile parameters) plus negative tests that no parameter authorises a request.
changes.why_not_weakening: The security outcome required is unchanged: no query parameter may influence authority, scope or object. Rejection remains one way to meet it; ignoring now has to be PROVEN per endpoint by behaviour (not by source reading), every handler under api/ must be classified (inventory test fails on a new endpoint), and the duplicate-parameter rule (P2) is untouched. Nothing that previously failed now passes: the five endpoints were MISSING_EVIDENCE, never compliant-by-assumption.

Four mutations that let a query grant authority, carry the secret, retarget the link or change the config are each killed.

changes.rationale: Owner decision (Phase 2D): P2 (constant-time MAC compare) and P3 (algorithm/key not selectable) are implementation invariants. They are marked evidence_basis STRUCTURAL and allowlisted in profile.structural_property_rule, so executable static evidence at the exact call site may satisfy them at E1 and is then reported as structurally verified. changes.why_not_weakening: The control minimum stays E4 and P1 still needs E4 known-bad proof. The exception is limited to exactly these two properties by an exhaustive allowlist (any other STRUCTURAL marker or misplaced structural evidence is a framework error, self-tests U1-U4). In this phase both properties ALSO reached behavioural E4 (EV-TOKEN-MAC + EV-KB-TOKEN-MAC), so the structural rule is not load-bearing for the PASS.

Framework weakness found while building CR-VERIFY-004 evidence: the type cap (F-2C-3) allowed any item declared type real-system to reach E5, so a plain sequential node test relabelled real-system could satisfy a real-concurrency control. Fixed: reproducible real-system evidence must require a non-node capability (REAL_SYSTEM_WITHOUT_INFRASTRUCTURE); fixture T2. All 7 existing real-system items require postgres - no status changed.

Application, Low. noContractCodeByQuorum (src/contract-signature.mjs) uses viem getCode, which returns undefined both for a real 0x answer and for an answer without result; `?? '0x'` turns both into "no contract code". If both providers answer without result (missing, null, empty 200 body), a Safe/contract wallet is treated as EOA: api/dashboard.mjs freshAuthorityRequired skips the fresh Safe confirmation for legacy sessions without kind (Telegram disconnect, sign out everywhere), and src/bot.mjs walletWideFromChatAllowed lets a (possibly stale) Telegram chat run the wallet-wide unlink/revocation. Requires two independent TLS providers to return such answers simultaneously. Fix direction: call eth_getCode via client.request and accept only a hex string result (CODE_HEX), treating undefined/null as malformed (provider not ok). Not fixed in Phase 2D.

P1 requires a committed mutation harness for EACH security fix. Enforcement is proven (fixtures X1, X2, P: an E4 control cannot PASS without a KILLED behavioural mutation), but no inventory of security fixes exists to show every fix maps to an E4 control. Decision needed: define "security fix" as the set of release-blocking E4 controls (clarification) or build a fix register (e.g. AGENT-SEC/AUDIT/META-AUDIT ids -> control/mutation). Stays MISSING_EVIDENCE.

P1 (each concurrency control has a real-Postgres test) is a meta-property of the framework; its evidence is framework behaviour (fixtures T, T2; reduced-environment verify shows the CONC controls fall to MISSING without Postgres), i.e. behavioural E3. The control demands E5 real-system, which framework evidence cannot be without a relabel. Decision needed: lower CR-VERIFY-004 to E3 as a versioned THRESHOLD_REDUCTION for a meta-control, or accept it as permanently MISSING. Stays MISSING_EVIDENCE.
Stop condition B (real application finding F-2D-2) reached during CR-PROVIDER-003. Not attempted: CR-RESOURCE-001, CR-INPUT-004, CR-BROWSER-004.

finding.root_cause: noContractCodeByQuorum used viem publicClient.getCode(), which returns undefined both for a real "0x" answer and for a JSON-RPC answer without result (missing, null, empty HTTP 200 body); the fallback `?? '0x'` then turned UNKNOWN into the positive statement "no bytecode".
finding.code_change: src/contract-signature.mjs noContractCodeByQuorum: read eth_getCode raw via client.request({ method: 'eth_getCode', params: [address, 'latest'] }) and accept only a string matching the existing strict CODE_HEX; no fallback. Same block tag, same dual-provider quorum, nothing else changed.
finding.before_behavior: Both providers answering without result -> true ("no contract code"): a legacy Safe dashboard session skipped fresh Safe authority for sign-out-everywhere and Telegram disconnect, and a (possibly stale) Telegram chat ran the wallet-wide revocation for the Safe.

versions.summary: Phase 2F: application finding F-2F-1 recorded as a VIOLATION of CR-RESOURCE-001 P1 (stop condition B, not fixed); remaining controls not attempted.

changes.reason: Application, Low. api/dashboard.mjs: for dashboard sessions without kind (issued before 2026-10-14, valid at most 7 days, i.e. until about 2026-10-21), freshAuthorityRequired calls noContractCodeByQuorum (eth_getCode at Alchemy AND Infura). On POST {action} this runs after the per-IP limit (20/600 s) but BEFORE the per-wallet limit and with no global limit; on DELETE (sign-out everywhere, ?telegram=1) after only the per-IP limit (10/600 s). A holder of one valid legacy session can rotate IPs to drive unbounded provider requests (cost/quota amplification; exhausted quotas make Safe login and ERC-1271 checks fail closed for everyone). Fix direction: apply the per-wallet and a global action budget before freshAuthorityRequired on both paths (or decide legacy sessions without RPC). Not fixed in Phase 2F.
